purpose: The "three ways to start" band of a product page: a centered section title with up to two calls to action, over a bento grid where every cell is an illustration above a bold-led sentence and one affordance — a link button or a copy button that puts a prompt on the clipboard. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-widgets', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `frame-box`, `bento-grid`, `illustration` and `button-highlight`.
useWhen: To offer the same outcome through two or three entry points (agent, console, terminal), each with its own next step.
avoidWhen: For reasons without an action per cell → use `feature-tiles`.
For a long argument per feature → use `feature-scroll`.
related: bento-grid` — the grid the cells are laid in.
button-highlight` — the copy affordance a cell renders when it carries `copy`.
bestPractices: Give each item exactly one of `action` (a link) or `copy` (text to put on the clipboard).
Keep `copy.text` self-contained; it is what the reader pastes into their agent.
Set `anchor` when a hero button scrolls to this band.
